The Florida State Seminoles will travel to Louisville to take on the Cardinals in Week 6 of the 2026 regular season. The game is set for Friday, October 9, 2026, at L&N Federal Credit Union Stadium in Louisville, Kentucky, and will be broadcast on ESPN. Florida State enters this contest with a 3-2 overall record, including a 0-1 mark on the road. Florida State is coming off a dominant 38-7 victory over the Virginia Cavaliers, showcasing their ability to control the game on the ground with 282 rushing yards. Despite their strong home performances, the Seminoles have struggled on the road. They will look to secure their first away win of the season against a conference opponent. The Louisville Cardinals, with a 2-3 record, are looking to bounce back after a narrow 31-28 loss to North Carolina State. Louisville has shown strength at home with a 2-1 record, including a high-scoring 41-31 victory over SMU. As they prepare to host Florida State, the Cardinals aim to leverage their home-field advantage to improve their conference standing. Louisville vs Florida State At a Glance (Week 6) Game Date and Time: Friday, October 9, 2026 at 7:00 PM Venue: L&N Federal Credit Union Stadium in Louisville, KY — Outdoor Field TV Channel: ESPN Florida State Record: 3-2 overall, 0-1 on the road Louisville Record: 2-3 overall, 2-1 at home Game Odds: Louisville -180, Florida State +149, Spread - Louisville -4 (-111) Louisville Cardinals Prepare for a Showdown at Home Offensive Performance The Louisville Cardinals have been effective on the offensive end this season, currently ranking 15th nationally with 193 points scored. Their passing game, led by quarterback Lincoln Kienholz, has been particularly strong, accumulating 1,437 yards and ranking 18th. The rushing attack has also contributed significantly, with 1,049 yards placing them 22nd in the nation. Keyjuan Brown and Isaac Brown have been instrumental in the ground game, combining for nearly 700 rushing yards. In the air, Tre Richardson has been the go-to target, amassing 445 receiving yards. The offense's ability to move the chains is evident with 117 first downs, ranking 16th nationally. Defensive Struggles On the defensive side, the Cardinals have faced challenges, allowing 146 points and ranking 97th in the nation. However, they have been impressive in creating turnovers, ranking 5th with 4 interceptions and 6th with 3 fumbles recovered. The defense has also generated pressure, recording 8 sacks to rank 14th. Despite these efforts, the Cardinals will need to tighten their coverage and improve their tackling to reduce the points allowed. Players like Antonio Watts, who is out with a knee injury, will be missed as the team seeks defensive consistency. Recent Form and Injuries Louisville enters this game with a 2-3 record in their last five games, most recently losing to North Carolina State 31-28. Injuries have been a concern, with several key players like Kris Hughes and Antonio Watts unavailable. Additionally, several players are questionable, which could impact depth and performance against strong opposition. Travis Egan and Sam Secrest are among those listed as questionable, potentially affecting both the offensive and defensive units. The Cardinals will need contributions from their depth to overcome these setbacks. Key Players to Watch Lincoln Kienholz remains a pivotal figure for the Cardinals, with over 1,394 passing yards and 9 touchdowns. His connection with Tre Richardson and Lawayne McCoy will be crucial in stretching the field and finding the end zone. On special teams, Carson Hilbert has been reliable, converting 6 field goals and 20 extra points this season. His accuracy could be a difference-maker in tight games. My play is the Seminoles getting the points. Louisville's close games are the entry point here. The Cardinals are 2-3, and all three losses have come by exactly three points: 41-38 to Ole Miss in Nashville, 30-27 at home to Wake Forest and 31-28 at NC State last week. Jeff Brohm's team scores, averaging 38.6 points per game, but it hasn't been able to pull away from anyone with a pulse. A team whose games keep landing on a field goal is a team you want to take points against. Louisville's defense is the reason those games stay close. The Cardinals allow 29.2 points per game (113th nationally), and their pass defense ranks 130th, giving up 266.8 yards per game. That's a unit Florida State can move the ball against. The Seminoles average 33.2 points per game and run for 194 yards per game behind Ousmane Kromah, and Ashton Daniels has shown he can push the ball downfield, throwing for 377 yards at Alabama. Florida State has also been more competitive than its record suggests. The Seminoles are 3-2, with a 27-24 loss to SMU and a 50-36 loss at Alabama. They've won their last two, including a convincing win over Virginia last week. Mike Norvell's team has an offense that can trade scores, and in a game with a total of 58.5, that's what it should come down to. The honest risk is Florida State on the road. The loss at Alabama was the Seminoles' 12th consecutive road loss dating back to 2023, and their own pass defense ranks 125th nationally. Lincoln Kienholz has thrown for more than 300 yards three times this season, and Louisville averages 287.4 passing yards per game. If the Cardinals get rolling through the air, this can get away. But Louisville's defense has given up at least 27 points in each of its three losses, and Florida State has the offense to keep pace. Realistic outcomes: Louisville 31, Florida State 28 (3-point margin, FSU covers +4); Florida State 30, Louisville 27 (FSU wins outright); Louisville 34, Florida State 30 (4-point margin, push); or Louisville 38, Florida State 27 (11-point margin, doesn't cover). Two of four scenarios cover for Florida State and one pushes. away.headline: Updated week 5 injury report adds to a growing issue within Florida State's defense
away.blurb: Florida State linebacker Noah LaVallee was downgraded from probable to out after there was previously hope he would play in Week 5. The Seminoles will be without four linebackers after the LaVallee announcement, as the freshman will join Izayia Williams, Blake Nichelson, and Daylen Green on the sidelines this week. Noah's brother and fellow linebacker, Caleb, is currently listed as probable for the upcoming game. Florida State's linebacker depth just took another hit with Noah LaVallee downgraded to out for Week 5 Florida State entered the game with a handful of players already confirmed to be out of the Week 5 game, but losing LaVallee particularly stings since he is a player filling in due to the injuries. LaVallee did not record any stats through the first three games, but began to work into the rotation against Central Arkansas with 21 snaps. The injury list is still rather long, even with a handful of players removed. Defensive back Quindarrius Jones and Caleb LaVallee are still listed as probable for the upcoming game against Virginia. Florida State and Virginia both released lengthy injury reports ahead of the Week 5 battle on Saturday. Both teams will be without a good chunk of the roster, but the key difference is that the Seminoles will be without multiple players at a vital position, and another player from the same position just joined that list. 2026 has not been the most productive season up to this point for Florida State, with a handful of players powering through bumps and bruises to compensate for the number of more serious injuries, particularly on defense. Starting safety Ashlynd Barker has been playing through a broken bone in his arm, although somewhat controversially , to make up for the shocking injury total. Without Noah and potentially Caleb in the picture, the slack will need to be picked up by the likes of Karon Maycock and AJ Cottrill. Maycock, a freshman, saw his first real action of the season against Central Arkansas and recorded three total tackles. Cottrill, on the other hand, saw action against SMU and Central Arkansas, totaling two tackles. During the Week 3 game against Alabama in Tuscaloosa, Florida State only played four linebackers and opted to use plenty of defensive backs. With Mikai Gbayor, Chris Jones, and Omar Graham Jr. all expected to play in Week 5, the Seminoles' staff might just give the remaining snaps at linebacker to the more experienced Cottrill. The only issue, however, is that Alabama and Virginia are far different teams in terms of how the offense attacks opposing defenses. Virginia is going to look to keep the football on the ground for most of the game. When combined with the play-action heavy passing attack, the Seminoles' linebackers could tire easily, which will force more of the remaining depth into the game. The updated injury report delivered a few positive bits of news for Florida State, as Ashlynd Barker, Chris Jones, KJ Kirkland, Donny Hiebert, and Xavier Tiller were all upgraded

away.headline: Virginia's lengthy injury report gives Florida State an obvious Week 5 game plan
away.blurb: The Seminoles essentially have to win this weekend versus the Virginia Cavaliers to get their season back on track. Mike Norvell is coaching for his job, and the only real way to do that is by essentially winning out in ACC play. This is an extremely daunting task, but the only way to eat an elephant is by taking it one bite at a time, and that is exactly what the game will be. Now that the injury reports have gone up for the matchup , it is easier to determine how this game will look. While both teams have a number of key players out, the focus for Florida State fans should be on the losses for Virginia on their defensive line. The biggest name to look for in that area is defensive tackle Jason Hammond. Hammond entered the season as one of the players with the most hype on the Virginia defensive front. This was supposed to be the year when Hammond finally took those next steps and solidified himself as one of the better linemen in the conference, but now it appears his return this season is in question. Kromah appears poised to remain the bell cow and should mostly see the opposing starters, but Wisner is where the lack of depth for Virginia will start to show itself. As the Cavaliers start to sub players out, FSU will try to spell Kromah with the equally-capable Wisner, and that is where FSU will need to force their will on a depleted opponent. The Wisner hype was perhaps a little too premature coming into the season based on his limited reps leading up to last week, but he has an easy path towards showing why the Seminoles put so much faith in him with a nice chunk of money on the transfer market. In the world of college football, teams will take whatever they can get if that gives them a chance to win. This is especially the case for a team like Florida State. Hammond absolutely leaves a hole on defense for the Cavaliers and his loss is further felt by the loss of depth across the front. Devon Baxter is the next most notable name to miss this weekend, largely a backup on the season, but several other depth players are also missing, leaving the Virginia rush defense susceptible. The good news for FSU is that their rushing attack is one of their biggest strengths, and Ousmane Kromah and Tre Wisner are more than up to the task . This game will still probably have some uphill sledding for the Noles to overcome, but this does at least display the obvious path for an FSU win and earn its first ACC win of the season. away.blurb: Miami has yet to play a conference home game this season, and the opening home game in league play should be against its most hated rival. The Hurricanes will return to primetime on Oct. 17 at Hard Rock Stadium at 7:00 p.m. to battle FSU at 7:00 p.m. ET on ESPN. "There's nothing more important than being where our feet are and being focused on the simple processes that we create, and really keeping people and things out of the equation. Right? I mean, you only have a limited amount of time, a limited amount of kilobytes in your own computer, right? Upstairs between the ears. The Miami Hurricanes are on a much-needed bye week, with several injuries starting to hinder the team. However, the start time for their next game has been announced as they prepare to face the Florida State Seminoles . For local radio audiences, the game will be broadcasted on 104.3 WQAM. The Seminoles are still holding on to a team that has some star talent but clumsy execution at times. However, Miami is still learning what kind of team it is. Moreover, there is no better time to express how they feel about the style of team they are playing against an in-state rival. "I think we're still learning," Cristobal said during his Monday press conference . "What I've learned is that this team really loves winning, and that they're willing to do the things necessary to win. This team learns and understands that we really can't allow anything to get in the way of a 1-0 process. To your question about processes, it's with all the distractions that surround our players in this modern college football world. "And you can't fill that space up with things that don't relate to what's important, right? And as it relates to the game, I think what this team has learned and is continuing to learn is that habits, choices, and decisions, as well as your practice and preparation, they all determine your game reality. So all focus on that and all effort on that." All that effort will go towards the Noles, who are coming off a victory against Virginia in one of the team's best overall group performances. Miami is coming off a statement-making win against Clemson, 41-13 on the road. However, instead of a bye week, FSU travels to take on the Louisville Cardinals, who continue to fight to find their identity after weeks of failing to live up to their talent. Miami will be watching patiently, dissecting what will be a fun matchup for both Florida programs. One minute, you're winning your conference opener on the road 31-13. The next minute, you're winning you're conference home opener 48-25. You don't look particularly great in either contest, but you cover the spread, hold up your end of the bargain, and sit 5-0 to start the year for the first time since 2016. That's the story of the Nebraska Cornhuskers. LINCOLN, NE - OCTOBER 3: Nebraska defensive back Jeremiah Charles (25) celebrates after blocking a punt in the first quarter of the game between the Maryland Terrapins and the Nebraska Cornhuskers on October 3, 2026, at Memorial Stadium in Lincoln, NE. (Photo by Nathanial George/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Nebraska took care of the Maryland Terrapins, albeit with one of the more dysfunctional beginnings to a game you'll see. A penalty on a (nearly) blocked punt that extended Maryland's drive, resulting in a field goal. Then after a three-and-out, an actual blocked punt that resulted in a Mekhi Nelson touchdown, his first of two in the game. Nebraska trained as much as 16-7, but still led 28-23 heading into halftime. The third quarter was a checkers match of moving a piece at a time, far away from your opponent. But the Huskers scored two seconds into the fourth quarter, and added two more touchdowns before the game ended. Meanwhile, the Nebraska defense held the Terps scoreless and relatively impotent after the 8:54 mark of the second quarter. Now it is time for the Huskers' biggest (and some may say first true) test of the season when the defending national champion Indiana Hoosiers make their way to Lincoln for Fox's Big Noon Kickoff. Curt Cignetti has his team in the top ten (top five in the Coaches' Poll), and even though there's no Fernando Mendoza, the Hoosiers are the only other team in the Bin ten to be undefeated. They have only been threatened once this year, when the Northwestern Wildcats of all teams gave them a scare, as the Hoosiers won that September 25 contest 29-23 at home. Indiana handled Rutgers this past weekend, and they mowed through their non-conference opponents (North Texas, Howard, and Western Kentucky) on easy mode. How will Nebraska perform against a rated team? Can they break the streak and knock off a ranked opponent? Would the rebuild fully be "on" if such a feat were to occur? Regardless of our collective thoughts on the outcome of the game, Vegas isn't counting on it. The line on FanDuel Sportsbook has Indiana as a 7.5-point favorite, marking the first time this season that Nebraska entered as the underdog. The over/under for the contest is 52.5 points. Bet your heart, but do so responsibly. Big Noon Kickoff between Nebraska and Indiana is Saturday at 11:00am Central, LIVE from Memorial Stadium, on Fox!

picks.headline: Early Indiana vs. Nebraska betting odds put Hoosiers on upset alert
picks.blurb: Early Indiana vs. Nebraska betting odds put Hoosiers on upset alert Skip to main content About Hoosiers News Indiana Basketball Indiana Football Indiana Baseball FanSided NCAA Sites Indiana Basketball Indiana Basketball Recruiting Indiana Football Indiana Football Recruiting Following a convincing 47-15 win over Rutgers on Saturday night, the Indiana Hoosiers are off to a 5-0 start and have extended their winning streak to 21 games. As we've seen before, Curt Cignetti tends to have his team playing better and better as the season goes on. Hoosier fans are hoping that trend continues, as the schedule gets a whole lot tougher from here. In Week 6, Indiana hits the road once again. This time the Hoosiers are heading west to take on the Nebraska Cornhuskers in a matchup between a pair of 5-0 teams. It starts a tough stretch of matchups for Indiana that also features battles against No. 5 Ohio State, at Michigan, vs Minnesota, and No. 19 USC. But first come the Cornhuskers. Early betting odds have been released for Saturday's matchup between the Hoosiers and Huskers, and it's clear that this is Indiana's toughest test so far this season. Oddsmakers expect a close game between the Hoosiers and Cornhuskers Indiana's first five games of the season have all seen the Hoosiers favored by at least three touchdowns. That changes in Week 6 against Nebraska. Via DraftKings Sportsbook, the Hoosiers are listed as 7.5-point favorites heading into Lincoln. Nebraska has been flying under-the-radar so far this season, but this gives Matt Rhule and company to make a serious statement. The total, or over/under, is listed at 51.5. Here is a closer look at the full Indiana vs Nebraska betting odds. Moneyline Indiana (-305) Nebraska (+245) Spread Indiana -7.5 (-105) Nebraska +7.5 (-115) Total Over 51.5 (-118) Under 51.5 (-102) Game odds refresh periodically and are subject to change. Indiana can't afford to overlook Nebraska in any way The Ohio State Buckeyes come to Bloomington in Week 7 for what is one of the most anticipated games of the entire college football season. Thus, this matchup at Nebraska can be considered a classic look-ahead spot for Indiana. But the Hoosiers can't afford to let their guard down. Nebraska has been a middle to bottom-tier Big Ten program in recent years. The Scott Frost era was brutal, and the Matt Rhule era hasn't been able to pick up much steam yet. However, the Huskers are playing solid football right now and are coming off back-to-back wins over Michigan State and Maryland by a combined score of 79-36. Memorial Stadium in Lincoln is always rocking, and in a matchup between a pair of undefeated teams, it is sure to be raucous environment once again. Indiana has faced Nebraska once under Cignetti's leadership, and it resulted in a lopsided 56-7 Hoosier win back on Oct. 19, 2024. Nebraska had 5-star freshman Dylan Raiola at QB in that matchup, and he is now off to Oregon. Anthony Colandrea is now leading the Husker offense, and he brings a solid mix of talent and experience to the table. Now in his fourth year as a college football starting quarterback, Colandrea has completed 65.7% of his passes for 1,142 yards and 13 touchdowns with just two interceptions this season. He's also added 249 yards and a pair of scores on the ground. With a much more experienced starter at the helm, the IU defense has to be ready for whatever Colandrea and the Cornhuskers throw at them. On paper, the Hoosiers have a talent edge over the Cornhuskers. They also have the best coach in the country leading the way. That should give IU fans plenty of confidence heading into this Week 6 clash. But still, it's imperative that the Hoosiers don't overlook the Huskers in any way. Kick-off is set for Noon ET on FOX. away.headline: Indiana Availability Report: Lee Beebe's Status and Who's Out vs Rutgers
away.blurb: Indiana Availability Report: Lee Beebe's Status and Who's Out vs Rutgers Skip to main content SI.COM Indiana could be without its leading rusher Saturday night when the Hoosiers take on Rutgers, with running back Lee Beebe Jr. listed as a game-time decision, per the Big Ten's availability report . Beebe, who rushed for 203 yards in Indiana's win over Northwestern last week, was a midweek addition to the availability report. His status headlines an otherwise encouraging final injury update for the Hoosiers, who had three players removed from the report ahead of their first road test of the season. Richard was listed as probable Friday before being removed from Saturday's report, putting him in line to handle the bulk of Indiana's rushing workload should Beebe be unable to go. Cuono, a second-year depth running back with 11 carries for 45 yards this season, would likely serve as Richard's primary backup in that scenario. True freshman Jayreon Campbell, who has rushed six times for 43 yards in limited action, is also available. Khobie Martin, meanwhile, remains out for the fourth consecutive game as he continues recovering from a forearm injury he suffered in Indiana's season opener against North Texas. Martin is expected to return around the midway point of the season. Indiana enters Saturday with a rushing attack ranked among the nation's top 10, although Beebe's potential absence would leave the Hoosiers without one of their most productive offensive weapons. Linebacker Rolijah Hardy, who was listed as probable Friday after suffering an injury late in his eight-tackle performance against Northwestern, was also removed from Saturday's availability report and is expected to play. A.J. Harris, Daniel Ndukwe among those ruled out Defensive end Daniel Ndukwe is also out, marking his first absence of the season. Ndukwe ranks second on the team with 4.5 tackles for loss, including 1.5 against Northwestern last week. Indiana still has considerable depth at edge, with Stephen Daley, Kellan Wyatt, Tobi Osunsanmi, Chiddi Obiazor and Josh Burnham available to help absorb his absence. Elsewhere, cornerback Carson Williams and wide receiver Lebron Bond remain out for the third and fourth consecutive games, respectively. Indiana and Rutgers are scheduled to kick off at 8 p.m. ET. Barney is second on the team in catches with 16 for 222 yards and 2 touchdowns. He’s also NU’s lead punt returner, so his absence could have been felt in several ways. Guthrie has played sporadically so far in 2028, though he has 8 tackles, an interception, and a 35-yard return. The only other Nebraska player whose status could have changed on Saturday was Carter Nelson , who remains listed as out for the second straight game. Jamal Rule's 'doubtful' status gives Nebraska a major concern with Maryland looming Earlier this week, the Nebraska football team’s backfield looked like it might be without Jamal Rule against Maryland . By Thursday, it looked like the Huskers might be without both Rule and Mekhi Nelson. On Saturday afternoon, it’s hard to say what the status of either running back is. If one or both running backs can’t go for Nebraska on Saturday afternoon, it looks like the run game will be in the hands of a pair of players who haven’t gotten a ton of carries this season in crunch time. Isaiah Mozee would likely be the starter against Maryland. The converted wide receiver is third on the team in rushes with 31 for 149 yards and a touchdown, but most of his carries have come when the Huskers had a game well in hand. When Mozee needs a blow, Kwinten Ives will most likely be the next guy in. Isaiah Mozee could lead Nebraska football backfield with Jamal Rule, Mekhi Nelson uncertain Ives only has 2 carries for 28 yards all season. Two Husker wide receivers have as many or more carries this season than Ives. Meanwhile, despite getting just 4 carries last week against Michigan State , Rule is tied with Nelson with 42 rushes. He also leads the team in rushing yards with 333 and has an incredible yards-per-carry average. He also has 6 total touchdowns. Nelson has 42 carries for 227 yards (5.4 YPC) with 2 touchdowns. Missing that production is certainly something Husker fans should be nervous about. On the other hand, Nebraska did get some good news for some other key players. Both safety Rex Guthrie and wide receiver Jacory Barney were spotted on the availability sheet all week, and neither was there Saturday. In other words, both are good to go against the Terps. home.headline: Jamal Rule's 'doubtful' status gives Nebraska a major concern with Maryland looming
home.blurb: On Monday, Huskers head coach Matt Rhule announced he wouldn't give any more player injury updates unless he absolutely had to, thanks to the new Big Ten availability report rules. The first availability report of the week was due at 7 pm on Wednesday and it turns out that Rule is listed as doubtful. At the end of the second quarter, Rule came back out of the Huskers’ locker room and tried running up and down the sideline. However, those who saw him try things out said he was still noticeably limping. The decision to keep him out for the rest of the contest was easier when NU scored a touchdown with just a second to go in the half, making the score 24-10. Jamal Rule doubtful for Maryland as Nebraska football chases first 5-0 start since 2016 In the past, Rhule has given injury updates during his Monday press conference during game week. However, following the lead of several other Big Ten coaches, he’s decided to wait until he absolutely has to tell the world whether a player is available. Wednesday’s availability report isn't the final word on Jamal Rule’s ability to play Saturday, though with him listed as doubtful, it’s clear he’s still feeling the effects of the injury. One need only look at the gamesmanship LSU head coach Lane Kiffin showed with his own availability report a few weeks back. In the first report, Kiffin said quarterback Sam Leavitt was “doubtful,” then gradually improved the prognosis. Leavitt started and played the whole game (and lost) against Ole Miss that week. After waiting and holding their breath since last Saturday evening, Nebraska football fans finally have the answer as to whether freshman phenom running back Jamal Rule will play against Maryland. Rule started the game against Michigan State last weekend but managed just four carries before he left the game with an apparent injury. For a time, it looked like Rule might come back in the second half. The potential absence of Rule is a massive one for the Cornhuskers, as he’s become one of the most electric players on the Nebraska football team early in the season. Not only that but he’s been one of the most electric freshmen in the entire country. Rule’s 333 rushing yards lead all first-year players, and he’s scored 6 touchdowns (5 rushing and 1 receiving) in just three full games. The phenom is averaging an incredible 7.9 yards per carry. The new rules require Big Ten coaches to release four availability reports. The next two will be on Thursday and Friday night, followed by a final, decisive one on Saturday morning. It seems unlikely that Matt Rhule would engage in that kind of gamesmanship for Nebraska’s showdown with Maryland, but something could change with Jamal Rule as the week goes on. picks.headline: Brent Brennan previews Mountaineers ahead of Arizona's trip to West Virginia
picks.blurb: 247Sports Logo 247Sports 247Sports Home FB Rec FB Recruiting Home Team Rankings Decommitments Scheduled Commits Player Rankings Player Search Recruiter Rankings Class Calculator All Time Top Recruits Transfer Portal BK Rec BK Recruiting Home Transfer Portal Top FB Transfers Latest FB Transfers By Position FB Transfers Top BK Transfers Latest BK Transfers By Position BK Transfers NCAA FB Teams College Team Talent Player Leaders NCAA BK Teams CBS SPORTS HQ 247Sports 247Sports Home News News News Latest News Boards Boards Lobby Arizona Basketball Forum Arizona Football Forum Arizona Baseball and Softball Football Football Scores Draft History 2027 NFL Draft Big 12 Schedules Big 12 Standings NCAA Player Leaders NCAA Team Leaders FB Rec FB Rec FB Recruiting Home Scholarship Distribution Latest Crystal Ball Official Visits All Time Recruits Basketball Basketball Scores BK Rec BK Rec BK Recruiting Home More More More VIP Membership Play Watch Watch CBS Sports College Football CBS Sports College Basketball Paramount+ Premium Forum Search Player Search Magnifying Glass Advanced player search Full site search Play Watch CBS Sports College Football Join OCTOBER SALE! 50% off annual VIP membership to AZ Band Cat Sports Trending VIP Five-star guard Adan Diggs breaks down Arizona official visit, previews upcoming trips Join Stay up to date on all the sports you love with CBS Sports HQ Arizona head coach Brent Brennan previews the West Virginia Mountaineers ahead of the Wildcats' trip Morgantown. (Photo: Mike Christy / Arizona Athletics) Arizona (4-1, 1-1) is right where folks thought it would be five games into the season. But the Wildcats haven't exactly won with style points, or looked like the team many thought they would at this point. But with a cross country game against one of the nation's most formidable rushing attacks led by former UA head coach Rich Rodriguez on the horizon, Brent Brennan isn't worried how flashy Arizona looks, how early the kickoff is, or the fact that the Wildcats are making one of the longest trips in the Big 12 this week. "This is what I think. I think if you let that be an excuse, it will be. I think if you let going on the road be an excuse, it will be," said Brennan during his Monday press conference. "So we're not in the excuse-making business. We're attacking the challenge ahead of us, which is playing a good West Virginia team at their place on Saturday at 9 a.m. Arizona time." As for the matchups on the field, Brennan knows Danny Gonzales' defense will have its work cut out for them for the second week in a row. Like Cincinnati , West Virginia is dominant running the football, but do it with a bit of a different style. The Mountaineers average a Big 12-best 294.0 yards per game and have one of the most explosive quarterback-running back duos in the league in Michael Hawkins Jr. and Cam Cook . Hawkins Jr. is tied for first in the country in rushing touchdowns, regardless of position, while Cook leads the Big 12 averaging 130.4 rushing yards per game. RichRod's team can light it up offensively and Brennan knows the Wildcats will have to be ready for an explosive ground game and the threat of Hawkins Jr. using his legs. "Yeah, [they're a] really offensively explosive, crazy tempo team. A lot of plus-one run game with the quarterback. They want to run the football, and they do a great job of that," said Brennan. "The running back is a total stud. He'd run for a ton of yards, lots of explosive plays. The quarterback is a stud, just a total badass, so that's going to be a great challenge for our defense." Arizona has faced a number of athletic, mobile quarterbacks already this season between NAU's Ty Pennington, WSU's Caden Pinnick , and most notably BYU's Bear Bachmeier . But Hawkins Jr. is unique according to Brennan, and someone who is going to give the Wildcats a run for their money – pun intended – on Saturday. "This one's different than those. This one's way different than those. This one is super twitchy, powerful acceleration," said Brennan. "This is a whole different challenge for us." While the offensive has garnered most of the media's attention since turning the page from Cincinnati, that's not stopping Arizona from keying in on what the Mountaineers do on defense, even if they've given up an average of 43 points per game through Big 12 play. "Defensively, they're multiple, high-pressure team. They're tough to plan for because there's a lot of variation there, because you're not really sure what you're going to get. They've been really stingy in the red zone, and they've been pretty good on third down. So again, big time football game on the road, tough environment. You got to get ready." Arizona is o-1 all-time against West Virginia after it failed to mount a comeback against the Mountaineers in Tucson in 2024. picks.blurb: West Virginia football expert previews the Arizona Wildcats game, makes a score prediction | Arizona Desert Swarm Skip to main content SB Nation SB Nation logo An Arizona Wildcats Community Arizona Desert Swarm October 6, 2026 Arizona Desert Swarm Notifications Notifications The Feed Sections Arizona Basketball Arizona Football Arizona Softball Arizona Recruiting Arizona Soccer Arizona Volleyball Arizona Baseball Arizona Gymnastics Arizona in the Pros Betting FanDuel College Football Odds FanDuel College Basketball Odds Arizona Football Odds Arizona Basketball Odds College Football Picks and Predictions College Basketball Picks and Predictions Login / Sign Up Search The Feed Sections Expand Arizona Basketball Betting Expand FanDuel College Football Odds Community Guidelines All communities Notifications Arizona Football RichRod Week! It’s not just Game Week, it’s RichRod Game Week! Arizona’s first trip to West Virginia will see it face off against former head coach Rich Rodriguez , who is back with the Mountaineers for a second go-around. Rodriguez coached there from 2001-07 before going to Michigan for three years and then spending 2012-17 with the Wildcats. The current West Virginia team is on a 2-game skid, losing a 45-42 shootout at Iowa State last weekend after falling at home to Oklahoma State in its Big 12 opener. To better understand RichRod’s squad, we reached out to Dillon Clark of SB Nation sister site The Smoking Musket for some insight and a score prediction. Below are his impressive answers to our mediocre questions: AZ Desert Swarm: West Virginia went 3-0 in nonconference play, including an impressive win over Virginia, but then has lost both conference games. What have been the main contributing factors to the backslide? Dillon Clark: “There has been a significant increase in competition in Big 12 play compared to our nonconference schedule. The win against Virginia looked good at the time because they were ranked, but after their performance against Florida State last week I don’t think they are going to be anywhere near the top of the ACC again. Our defense hasn’t looked great all year but the wheels have come completely off in the last two games. We have given up over 1,200 yards of total offense in the last two games which equates to about 3/4 of a mile if you were wondering.” It’s to no one’s surprise in Wildcat Nation that a RichRod-coached team is running the ball well, but this production seems to be at another level. What’s been the key to the rushing success, and how do you think Arizona’s defense will try to neutralize this? “We spent a ton of money in the portal on a quarterback, running back and several offensive linemen. Michael Hawkins Jr. has exceeded expectations at the quarterback position for us averaging over 100 yards per game on the ground 6.2 yards per carry. Many of his best runs are coming off of pass plays that would have resulted in a sack or throw away for most other QBs so when you turn those negative plays into big positives it really shows up on the stat sheet. One of the biggest surprises to me has been his elusiveness in the red zone and the ability to make people miss. I knew he was fast, I didn’t realize how shifty he is. Cam Cook has also produced at a high level in the RB position. He is such a tough runner. His yards after contact and broken tackles are what really sets him apart. Even though he isn’t what I would call fast, he has consistently popped big runs. He gets stronger as the game goes on and the majority of his yardage has come in the second half of games.” Quarterback Michael Hawkins Jr. is tied for the FBS lead with 11 rushing touchdowns, but how is he as a passer? Would you trust him if he had to be one-dimensional in this way? “I think it’s fair to call Michael Hawkins Jr. a streaky passer. The last three games he has started out looking a bit shaky in the pass game with off target throws. In two of the three he eventually settled in and made plays with his arm. The completion percentage against Iowa State was a bit lower than you like, but he did have a couple drops and throw aways in there. I have confidence in him as a passer, my bigger question is can our receivers get open consistently in a situation where we have to throw the ball, and can we establish an intermediate passing game? It feels like our passing game at times this year has been all or nothing. The drive-extending, possession-style passing game has not been sharp. I don’t blame that on Michael Hawkins as much as I do on play calling and scheme. I have a hard time seeing anyone making him purely one dimensional as a passer this year. Teams may shut down our traditional running game, but we have seen teams put multiple spies on him in the past few weeks and he is still escaping the pocket for chunk yardage.” The Mountaineers’ defensive numbers are not good, ranking last in the Big 12 in almost every category. Is this a talent issue, a problem with the scheme, or both? “In order to be as bad as we have been, it has to be all of the above right? Our tackling is bad. Missed assignments on nearly every possession.We can’t get pressure on the quarterback. When we are in the right place we end up with a pass interference penalty. It’s rough all around. There has been a lot of talk on if Zac Alley’s reputation as a sort of ‘mad scientist’ on defense could be part of the problem. It’s really hard to argue against that when you see us consistently confused on pre-snap alignments. The biggest concern is that we are struggling in every aspect. Scoring defense, rushing defense, pass defense, total yardage, it doesn’t matter which stat you look at, we are at or near the bottom. The only hope is that potentially our two best defenders just became eligible last week. Jacorey Thomas and Jason Chambers should help plug some holes in what has been a leaky secondary. There is only one way for us to go from here.” How has the second coming of RichRod been so far in your estimation? Have there been any classic moments in terms of his antics? “After the Virginia win in Week 3 the vibes around the WVU fan base were as high as I’ve seen them in a very long time. That game brought back a lot of great memories from Rich Rod’s first tenure here and it felt like the sky was the limit. The last two weeks have put a damper on the mood though the fact that the offense has been producing at a high level still does take some of the blame off of him. The Rich Rod offense is back and it’s humming, but how did he not see this coming with the defense? There was definitely a group of the fanbase that didn’t want him back, and those voices are getting louder with each loss. I think he has shown enough so far that the majority of the fan base still believes he can get this right. We love that he holds players accountable in the moment, and it gives us hope that he can turn this thing around.” Prediction time. Does Arizona beat its former coach and get a big conference road win or do the Mountaineers hold serve at home? Give us a score prediction. “We have the worst defense in the Big 12. You have one of the best offenses. We are coming off of two straight brutal conference losses. You are coming off of a dominant win against a previously undefeated Cincinnati team. In other words, we have you right where we want you. 45-31 Mountaineers get back on track at home.” Download the new SB Nation app All of your communities in one place. Oct 3, 2026 Updated Oct 3, 2026 AMES — Cody Jackson transferred to Iowa State last winter in search of his fourth fresh start. The talented transfer wide receiver found it, but catches proved tough to come by. Until Saturday, when the former Oklahoma, Houston and Tarleton State player erupted for 160 receiving yards in the Cyclones’ momentum swing-filled 45-42 triumph over West Virginia at Jack Trice Stadium. “I trusted in God, number one, and trusted in my coaches (and) my teammates,” said Jackson, who didn’t record a catch in ISU’s first two games, but now has 12 receptions in the past two games. “Not having my head down. Keeping my head high. Keeping a smile on my face every day and coming in and working at practice.” Jackson’s first grab on Saturday for the Cyclones (3-2, 1-1 Big 12) turned into a 46-yard touchdown on a halfback toss from Aiden Flora. His other seven receptions against the Mountaineers (3-3, 0-2) came during a tense second half, and many fueled three straight scoring drives that helped ISU preserve the win. “He did a great job finding open windows and attacking the ball in the air,” Cyclones quarterback Jaylen Raynor said. Jackson notched 92 yards after the catch and often adjusted his routes as Raynor improvised amid amped up West Virginia pressure. His 43-yard catch on third-and-six early in the fourth quarter set up Kyle Konrardy’s 35-yard field goal that gave ISU a 31-28 lead. And Jackson’s 15-yard grab on the Cyclones’ final scoring drive ended in one of Flora’s three rushing touchdowns. Flora’s now averaging 8.1 yards per carry and has rushed for 600 yards and six touchdowns. “(He’s) a great leader,” Jackson said. “He can do everything, like you could see. away.blurb: "We're at a point where we're going into conference play and we know we've got to play better," Hall told us at his weekly media conference. "We've not played our best yet. That's a negative, but also a positive that our best is still out there. You should get better as the season goes on....We feel like we're a much better football team right now than we were last time we talked to you (two weeks ago)," Expect the highly anticipated return of last year's breakout running back Jamauri McClure . The then-freshman sensation rushed for 540-yards, though really being used from about the midway point in the year on. He averaged 6.5-yards every time he touched the ball in 2025. McClure was injured during Fall practice getting surgery on his left foot to repair damage done. He's been sidelined all this year, with the Wave targeting the American opener as his season debut. Receiver Zycarl Lewis , who was hurt during the Duke game, is set to return as well, recovering from a leg injury. Though Hall listed both tight end Ty Thompson and linebacker Chris Rodgers as doubtful for Saturday, fans should not plan on either of them contributing this weekend. Thompson is nursing a leg injury that has forced him to miss extended time, and Rodgers has a foot injury that is putting the star backer on the sidelines for the foreseeable future. Tulane Prepares for Army Option, Welcomes Back 2025 Star RB from Injury Skip to main content On SI The Tulane football team opens the defense of its American Conference 2025 championship on Saturday with a trip to West Point to visit the United States Military Academy. Kickoff from Michie Stadium is set for 11:00 a.m. CT and can be seen on the CBS Sports Network. After a bye week to rest up and prepare, Green Wave head coach Will Hall is feeling good about his squad's preparedness. "The advantages of when our bye week fell is it is right smack dab in the middle of our season," Hall shared Tuesday. "We had five weeks of fall camp, then four games. That's nine weeks. Now we've got a bye week and eight games left. So, it's right in the middle. It is right before conference play and it's right before we play an option team. I think those are advantages The league opener is like a new season for Hall and his team, as they get ready for what is essentially a restart to their season. "We know how important it is to get off on the right foot and be 1-0 in conference play," Hall said Tuesday, "so our young men are taking that very seriously. But also we all want to play (well) for us and I want us to play (well) for our players. I want our players to play better, so in turn they get more touches and get more accolades for themselves and they get the the harvest for all the work they've put in. You can see it. away.headline: Army football seeks bounce back in return to home action vs. Tulane
away.blurb: News Sports Life Opinion Real Estate Advertise Obituaries eNewspaper Legals COLLEGE Army football seeks bounce back in return to home action vs. Tulane Ken McMillan Middletown Times Herald- Record Updated Oct. 6, 2026, 9:47 a.m. ET In the end, Army's 21-19 loss at Louisiana Tech on Saturday night was just a non-conference game and didn't affect the American Conference standings. However, the Black Knights are having trouble building on positives. "It's very hard to play perfect,'' said Monken, who also points out the margin for error is slim for his West Point teams. "We're going to strive to it.'' Monken pointed out that Army had too many missed assignments, played with poor fundamentals at times and didn't help themselves with six penalties, but he's not given up on the squad. A dominant win over Bryant in the opener, followed by a crushing late loss at home to South Florida. A tough road win over Temple, followed by a stumbling loss as a small favorite at Louisiana Tech , dropping the Black Knights to 2-2. "We're not going to let this game kind of derail our season,'' said senior center and co-captain Brady Small. "We're going to go back, we're going to watch some film, we're going to learn and get ready for Tulane, another conference game. So just use this as fuel to the fire to get us a win at home.'' Army is a three-point favorite over Tulane for Saturday's noon ET start. Army is 1-1 in American action, and needs a win vs. the Green Wave to stay in contact with the 1-0 leaders: Florida Atlantic (4-1 overall), Memphis (4-1), Texas San Antonio (4-1), Alabama Birmingham (3-2) and North Texas (3-2). Army will face FAU and Memphis but not the other three this season. "Honestly, we've just got to attack the adversity at hand,'' said back Samari Howard. Photo By - Reuters Connect. Texas defensive end Colin Simmons (1) celebrates with the Golden Hat following the Red River Rivalry. One of college football's best-known rivalries returns for its 122nd edition in Week 6, as Texas and Oklahoma meet at the Cotton Bowl in Dallas at 3:30 p.m. ET (ABC), with the Texas State Fair taking place right outside. The Texas vs. Oklahoma rivalry , better known as the Red River Rivalry, has been played every season since 1929, with these two storied programs often blocking each other from winning a conference championship or, in modern times, reaching the College Football Playoff. Texas is the favorite and has won Red River in three of the last four years, making it a popular pick among college football analysts . Texas vs Oklahoma 2026 preview Steve Sarkisian (52-20) Head coach (record with school) Brent Venables (34-22) SP+ special teams Texas vs Oklahoma odds Texas vs Oklahoma prediction The Red River Rivalry hasn't been kind to Oklahoma head coach Brent Venables. Since he took over the Sooners in 2022, he's 1-3 straight up and ATS against Texas . In those three wins for Steve Sarkisian, the Longhorns beat Venables' Sooners by an average of 32.3 points. That includes a 49-0 win in 2022, the third-largest blowout in the Red River Rivalry history. Even last year, when Oklahoma made the College Football Playoff and Texas didn't, the Longhorns beat the Sooners, 23-6. That was due in large part to a poor performance from ohn Mateer , who led Oklahoma to just 258 total yards while throwing three interceptions and accounting for six turnover-worthy plays. This year shouldn't be much different, with Mateer back behind center and ranking top 10 in the country in turnover-worthy play rate (6%). Mateer is the biggest reason why OU has the lowest offensive success rate in the SEC (39.2%) and is 109th in the country in PPG (22.0). This year's Texas defense is even better, too, sitting No. 3 in net adjusted EPA per play, No. 11 in success rate (36.5%), and No. 16 in havoc rate (20.6%). Texas has the talent to hand Oklahoma its fourth double-digit Red River Rivalry loss of the Venables era. Score prediction: Texas 24, Oklahoma 13 Who are the stars of Texas vs Oklahoma 2026? Arch Manning, QB, Texas Though Arch Manning hasn't played up to his preseason Heisman Trophy odds , he is one of the most talented quarterbacks in the country. The former No. 1 recruit is a few weeks removed from leading an improbable comeback against Ohio State and ranks 11th in the Power Four in big-time throw rate (5.9%). Last year against a top-notch Sooners defense, Manning finished with an 89.5 QBR and a 91.3% adjusted completion percentage. If he can be that efficient against OU again this year, Texas should cruise to a win, and Manning will reignite the chatter around him as the potential No. 1 pick this April. Isaiah Sategna III, WR, Oklahoma There isn't much to get excited about with this Oklahoma offense, but Isaiah Sategna III is a future NFL player and by far the Sooners' scariest playmaker. In his first season with the program last year after transferring from Arkansas, Sategna led the Sooners in yards from scrimmage by a large margin (989) and was third in the SEC in YAC (524). He's been the lone bright spot again this year, leading the team in scrimmage yards (284) while being one of the country's best punt returners. For OU to pull off the upset, it needs its superstar slot receiver to torch Texas. Trevor Goosby/Melvin Siani, OT, Texas While Manning has been sacked 10 times in four games, that has more to do with his indecisiveness than it does with his offensive line. The Longhorns' signal caller has the 12th-highest time to throw in the country (3.13), and despite that, his star offensive tackles have allowed a combined 11 pressures and two sacks. Coming into the season, Trevor Goosby was viewed as one of the country's best tackles and a potential first-round pick, but Melvin Siani flew under the radar. Siani, a Wake Forest transfer, has been as good as Goosby and is playing himself into the first-round conversation. The Sooners are 12th in the country in havoc rate (21.6%), so Texas needs Goosby and Siani to keep Manning clean to win. David Stone/Taylor Wein, DL, Oklahoma Oklahoma's most talented player is David Stone, and its most disruptive is Taylor Wein. Stone came into the season as a potential first-round pick and Wein as a potential top-100 pick. While Stone hasn't had the impact that was expected of him (just three pressures, two TFLs, 0.5 sack), he's the Sooners' X-factor with his twitch and active hands. At his best, the former five-star recruit is one of the most disruptive interior defensive linemen in the country. Wein, meanwhile, has been OU's best defender (14 defensive stops, 4.5 TFLs). The defensive line duo will need to create havoc against Texas and pressure Manning if Oklahoma's going to have any shot at an upset. Last year in Red River, Stone and Wein combined for five pressures and four TFLs. Colin Simmons, EDGE, Texas There's an argument that Colin Simmons has been the best defensive player in college football through the first few weeks. The projected top-five pick has been borderline unblockable, and in Texas' last game against Tennessee, he set the single-game school record for sacks (5.5). Simmons is top 10 in the Power Four in pressures (18) and is second nationally in sacks (7.5). He's as explosive as he is relentless and will be a massive problem for Oklahoma, especially with how turnover-prone Mateer has been this season. Last year, the Sooners couldn't stop his disruption as he tallied 2.5 sacks to win the Longhorns the Golden Hat. Peyton & Eli Bowen, DB, Oklahoma Everyone knows Peyton and Eli Manning, and their burnt orange-wearing nephew, Arch, but there's another pair of brothers named Peyton and Eli with NFL futures suiting up on the other side of the Red River Rivalry. Peyton (Oklahoma's starting safety) and Eli Bowen (Oklahoma's starting cornerback) are both from Texas, but don the crimson and cream of the Sooners. They're also two of the best defensive backs in the SEC and tied for the lead in forced incompletions at Oklahoma this season (three). Neither is allowing an NFL QB rating above 65.0 when targeted either, and they could be a huge thorn in Arch's side. OU needs the Bowen brothers to lock down the back end of its defense in Red River this year. Texas vs Oklahoma rivalry history: Red River Rivalry 8 (1940-1947) Longest win streak 6 (1952-1957) Largest margin of victory 977-401-34 (.704) Program record 962-355-53 (.722) Claimed national titles (recognized) Conference championships Heisman winners Consensus All-Americans Weeks in the AP Poll Weeks at No. 1 Bowl games (record) NFL draft picks First-round picks This is one of college football's most competitive rivalries because both Texas and Oklahoma have had national success . It also adds to the lore that Texas has been the more successful team in the Red River Rivalry, while Oklahoma has had more national success over the last few decades. Like a river, the rivalry has ebbed and flowed for decades, with Hall of Fame coaches taking over, ending losing streaks, and winning national championships. Red River is one of the defining rivalries in all of sports. The rivalry began in 1900 with a 28-2 win for Texas , and the Longhorns wouldn't lose to Oklahoma until the eighth meeting in 1905, when the Sooners won 2-0. Texas dominated the rivalry ini

As of today, it has been 1,094 days since OU reached the end zone, dating back to the Sooners' 2023 upset (fluke) win over the Horns. However, even as Texas has held Oklahoma to just three field goals over the last two Red River Rivalries, the Longhorns haven't exactly put on offensive showcases . This year, the expectations for the offenses aren't all that different, and the oddsmakers have the 2026 Red River Rivalry as low-scoring as the last couple of seasons. picks.headline: No. 1 Texas vs. Oklahoma preview: Reeling Sooners look to pull off upset
picks.blurb: No. 1 Texas vs. Oklahoma preview: Reeling Sooners look to pull off upset | Burnt Orange Nation Skip to main content SB Nation SB Nation logo A Texas Longhorns Community Burnt Orange Nation October 6, 2026 Burnt Orange Nation Notifications Notifications Get The App Sections Texas Longhorns Recruiting Betting FanDuel College Football Odds FanDuel College Basketball Odds Texas Football Odds Texas Basketball Odds College Football Picks and Predictions College Basketball Picks and Predictions Community Guidelines Login / Sign Up Search Get The App Sections Expand Texas Longhorns Recruiting Betting Expand FanDuel College Football Odds All communities Notifications Texas Longhorns Football The Sooners head to Dallas with a struggling offense and stingy defense. Fresh off a bye week with a 4-0 record, the No. 1 Texas Longhorns head up I-35 for the annual Red River Rivalry against the Oklahoma Sooners, who have struggled thus far in 2026 — Oklahoma has a 2-2 record on the year and has failed to score more than 14 points in each of their last three contests. On paper, this is a matchup that should favor the Longhorns, but if history has shown anything, nothing matters once these two teams take the field at the Cotton Bowl. Scoring points against the Oklahoma defense is doable but will undoubtedly be the biggest challenge facing the Longhorns. “This is always a unique game because you can take record, stats, and all those things and throw them out the window,” Texas head coach Steve Sarkisian said on Monday. “You’ve got to play the game and you’ve got to play the game the right way.” The struggles for the Sooners start on the offensive end. Returning quarterback John Mateer has failed to effectively move the ball through the air and the running attack ranks 131st in the FBS in yards per game. Second-year offensive coordinator Ben Arbuckle has made his money with Mateer at the helm, a partnership that is now in it’s fourth year and dates back to their time together at Washington State, but is currently testing the patience of Oklahoma fans given the offense’s lack of scoring. “Coach Venables, I know he’s probably sitting there thinking he wishes the record was a little bit different, but man, his teams play hard, and this team’s no different,” Sarkisian said. “They play hard. They’re an excellent defensive football team. They’ve got draft picks all over on the defense. Offensively, they’ve got playmaking ability similar to us. They’re trying to find their way to to find that level of consistency. But one thing I can be assured of — we’re going to get their best shot, and so I think it’s important for us that we focus on what we need to do so that we can play our best football.” With concerns across the Sooner offense, this year’s rendition will likely be determined by the success of the Longhorns finding the end zone in the Cotton Bowl. If the Longhorns can score points, things could get out of hand. Here’s what to expect on Saturday. As mentioned, the Oklahoma offense is headed by Arbuckle and Mateer. Arbuckle is a young and forward-thinking coordinator with a track record of quarterback development and roots in the Air Raid. At 31 years old, he has already helped develop Bailey Zappe, Austin Reed, and Cam Ward. His offense utilizes tempo and the run game to stretch defenses and create passing windows. With the athleticism of Mateer and the inability to create an impactful rushing attack otherwise, Arbuckle has adapted the offense to feature a quarterback run threat on nearly every play. Averaging just 22 points per game and coming off a bye week, a few new wrinkles are all but guaranteed from Arbuckle on Saturday. Much has been made of Mateer’s play at quarterback this season. The returning starter for the Sooners came into the season with lofty expectations after a turnover-prone 2025 season. Through four games, his play has been disappointing, prompting Venables to admit that he considered benching his starting quarterback at halftime of the Georgia loss. Mateer has completed 66.1 percent of his passes for 883 yards and eight touchdowns while adding 41 carries for 76 yards. However, Mateer has turned the ball over six times in four games, including three first-half turnovers last week against Georgia. Pro Football Focus has tracked eight throws by Mateer as turnover worthy this season. Holding on to the ball is priority number one for Mateer, who has looked rattled in the pocket the season. He’s missed reads, held on to the ball, and fired inaccurately on numerous occasions. Keeping Mateer uncomfortable sets the tone for the Texas defense. Nearly everything else is downstream of whether the Longhorn front can keep him guessing and rushed. Keeping Mateer’s legs out of the game will be another key for Texas — if Mateer can extend plays or effectively pick up first downs on designed runs, things get significantly more complicated for the Longhorn defense. Expect a heavy dose of quick, high-completion throws to start the game in order to neutralize the Texas pass rush and get Mateer into a rhythm. The lead back for the Sooners is junior Lloyd Avant. Avant is a 5’10, 212-pound ball carrier from Humble who has racked up 164 yards and a touchdown on 42 carries (3.9 YPC). A transfer from Colorado State, Avant was expected to compete for snaps with Tory Blaylock, but has been thrust into the starting role due to Blaylock’s hamstring injury. Against UTEP, Avant looked strong, rushing for 79 yards on 15 carries; however, in the three games since, he has carried the ball 27 times for just 85 yards. Blaylock came into the season as the leading back, but is recovering from injury. He’s gotten a handful of carries, but its clear that the coaching staff does have not believe he is close to 100 percent. With an additional week to recover, it’s very possible that he contributes in a more meaningful way on Saturday. Regardless of who takes handoffs, improvement is needed on the ground. After finishing 113th in rushing offense last season, the Sooners are 133rd in yards per rush and t-134th with two rushing touchdowns on the season. Despite an offseason of revamping the rushing attack, things have regressed through four games. “It’s frustrating because I feel like I’m not doing my part,” said tight end Rocky Beers , via OU Insider . “There’s always one miss here, one miss there, and it’s costing us... We’ve just got to believe in our blocks and hold onto them as long as we can.” Getting back to running the ball was undoubtedly a point of emphasis over the bye week and something that the Longhorns will need to thwart on Saturday. Wide receiver Perhaps the most talented player on the Sooner offense is leading wide receiver Isaiah Sategna. A transfer from Arkansas, Sategna leads the offense in receptions (20), yards (267), and longest play from scrimmage (53). His two touchdowns are tied for the most on the team. Listed at 5’10, Sategna isn’t a huge target but can be dangerous. His quickness can generate missed tackles and additional yardage after the catch, so closing in quickly will be important come Saturday. Sategna forced 22 missed tackles last season and half of his receiving yards this season have come after the catch. Transfers Trell Harris and Parker Livingstone were brought in to supplement Sategna but neither has been effective thus far. Harris remains sidelined with an injury and Livingstone hasn’t been able to make a difference, though this will undoubtedly be a big game for him after transferring from Texas during the offseason. Stopping Sategna will be the key to keeping the wide outs locked down, a task that Longhorns defensive coordinator Will Muschamp has to feel good about. Veteran tight end Rocky Beers, a Colorado State transfer, has proved to be a reliable weapon for Mateer in the passing game, tallying 18 catches for 255 yards and two touchdowns this season, which is the best on the team outside of Sategna. One of three tight ends brought in from the portal by new position coach Jason Witten, Beers has looked the part this season. His route running creates windows for Mateer and he has enough size to be a matchup problem on smaller defenders. When Oklahoma makes it to the red zone, Beers is a frequent target, something that Texas will need to take away come Saturday. Offensive line The running game has struggled for the Sooners and a big reason for that falls on the shoulders of the offensive line. This group has failed to keep a clean pocket, generate push, and open running lanes. If Oklahoma hopes to turn things around offensively, the five up front will need to step up their performance, immediately. Against Georgia, the Oklahoma offensive line switched things up, sitting Eddy Pierre-Louis at guard in favor of Heath Ozaeta and Noah Best, but it made little difference. E’Marion Harris, the right tackle, still looked a step slow while star left tackle Michael Fasusi remains sidelined with a shoulder injury. I’d expect this group to get additional help in blocking from tight ends and running backs, as well as a heavy dose of plays designed to get the ball out of Mateer’s hand quickly. This group has yet to show anything special through four games, increasing pressure on longtime position coach Bill Bedenbaugh, whose tenure dates to the Bob Stoops era. The Oklahoma offense has sputtered to start the year. Poor quarterback play coupled with a lack of rushing attack and porous offensive line has resulted in little points being scored. With a bye week to prepare for the Longhorns, I’d expect a sharpened game plan out of the gate that features quick passes and unique ways to get the ball out of Mateer’s hands. For the Longhorn defense to find success, getting pressure is key. When Mateer feels the pass rush, he has shown an inability to make good reads and deliver accurate passes. Keeping him from feeling comfortable will be a point of emphasis for the Longhorns. Outside of Mateer, limiting Sategna and Beers is the next priority. Forcing someone besides these three players to make a difference should spell success for the Longhorns. For every concern about the offense, the defense boasts a strength. This unit has been salty thanks to a solid crop of returners despite a mediocre offense on the other side of the ball that can’t finish drives and turns the ball over. Moving the ball through the air against the Sooners has been particularly tough. Allowing 122.5 passing yards per game, the OU secondary ranks fourth in the country, and is led by returning producers that understand the scheme and have the physical talent to implement it successfully. Opponents convert 23.1 percent of third downs, the third best in the entire country, meaning staying ahead of the chains will be essential for the Texas offense. The best method to attack this defense has been via the run. Averaging 115.5 yards per game on the ground and 3.23 yards per carry, this aspect remains in the top third of the country but lags behind the stellar pass and third-down defense. Don’t be mistaken by the record or score against Georgia — the Oklahoma defense can get after it. Defensive line Up front, there are four players that Texas will need to handle — defensive ends Taylor Wein and Adepoju Adebawore, and tackles David Stone and Jayden Jackson. In the middle, Stone and Jackson are a formidable duo. Stone was one of the Sooners’ most highly-regarded returners after notching 43 tackles a year ago. Now in his third year at Oklahoma, the 6’3, 312-pound lineman will be looking for his first win in Dallas. Next to him, Jackson is quite the player. Last season, he tallied 28 tackles and 3.0 sacks, including being honored as the Outland Trophy National Player of the Week for his performance against Auburn. This duo up front has been a big reason why the defense has been stout thus far. away.blurb: Well, this week's message is along that exact same vein, with the Horns' head coach denying to provide any additional context ahead of releasing the first availability report of the week, which comes out at 7:10 p.m. CT on Wednesday evening. Both were listed as "OUT" on the final availability report for Week 4 , alongside defensive back Xavier Filsaime and offensive lineman Jordan Coleman. For now, one could hope (and reasonably assume, based on Sarkisian's message about getting healthier) that at least one of those players is ready for, or close to ready for, action in the rivalry game. 3 wrinkles in Texas's road win over Vols the Horns must iron out before the Red River Rivalry After nearly a week and a half since we last saw the Texas Longhorns take the field against the Tennessee Volunteers, many people were eager to hear how previously injured players had progressed over the bye. However, what should come as no surprise is that Texas head coach Steve Sarkisian had another idea in mind : no update. With star players like running back Hollywood Smothers, tight end Nick Townsend, and defensive lineman Justus Terry all missing time this season, Longhorn Nation has been eager to see their guys back in action. Unfortunately, we will have to wait to see what we should expect on Saturday. "I think we're healthier than we were a week ago at this time," Sarkisian said in his game preview press conference, continuing his refusal to share injury updates beyond what he puts in the SEC-mandated availability reports. Steve Sarkisian sticks to SEC availability report and nothing more On Monday of Week 4, before the Horns faced the Vols, Sarkisian expressed a similar sentiment, refusing to update members of the media on any lingering injuries, stating that "There's called an injury report in the SEC, so that's enough of the injury questions," Sarkisian said that week. Based on the final injury list from Texas's game against Tennessee, one could easily assume that Smothers will be good to go against the Oklahoma Sooners this weekend as the Horns prepare for the annual Red River Rivalry. The star running back was off the report just before kickoff and was seen on the sidelines in full pads, with his helmet on, but never entered the game against the Volunteers. However, when it comes to Terry and Townsend, your guess is as good as mine. Smothers is nursing a reported lower-leg injury suffered in practice, Townsend is healing up from a knee injury he sustained before Week 2's kickoff, Terry is recovering from a toe injury ahead of Week 2's game, Coleman hasn't played since Week 3, and Filsaime has yet to take the field this season. For right now, Texas fans (and Oklahoma fans) will have to wait to see what Texas's injury list looks like on Wednesday evening, because until then, Sarkisian is remaining tight-lipped about the health of his team. (Sara Diggins/Austin American-Statesman) Thomas Jones Wed, September 30, 2026 at 4:01 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads Texas basketball suffered a major preseason injury when guard Mikey Lewis broke a bone in his right foot this week in practice. He will undergo surgery Thursday in Austin and will likely miss "an extended period of time," according to a Texas spokesperson. A 6-foot-3 guard with three remaining years of eligibility, Lewis played at St. Mary's last season and earned All-West Coast Conference honors after averaging 13.9 points, 2.7 rebounds and 2.1 assists. He fills a roster need for an outside shooter, too; over his first two seasons, he made 126 of his 340 3-point shots for a long-distance rate of 37.1%. Lewis, an Oakland native, is part of a five-player transfer class that also includes former Auburn wing Elyjah Freeman , former Tennessee guard Amari Evans , former TCU power forward David Punch and former Colorado guard Isaiah Johnson . When healthy, he's expected to serve as a valuable shooting option of the bench as part of a guard rotation that also includes Johnson, Evans and a trio of freshmen in McDonald's All-American Austin Goosby , Bo Ogden and Joe Sterling. Ogden, the son of Texas general manager Chris Ogden, earned the Central Texas boys player of the year award lats season from the American-Statesman after leading Westlake High School to the state finals. home.blurb: Defensive tackle Justus Terry, defensive back Xavier Filsaime and offensive lineman Jordan Coleman were all unavailable against Tennessee, while tight end Nick Townsend had been listed as doubtful. Texas Injuries Could Shape Red River Matchup Against Oklahoma LonghornsRoundtable 446 Members • 1,680 Posts LonghornsRoundtable LonghornsRoundtable Featured stories Scott Wachter-Imagn Images Scott Wachter-Imagn Images Texas Injuries Could Shape Red River Matchup Against Oklahoma Timothy Hamm Partner Oct 4, 2026 6:14 PM Published Oct 4, 2026 6:14 PM Texas enters Oklahoma week healthier after its bye, but several key Longhorns remain worth watching ahead of Saturday’s Red River Rivalry in Dallas. More Videos Texas football enters Red River Rivalry week in a better injury position than it faced at Tennessee, but the Longhorns still have several important availability questions before Saturday’s showdown with Oklahoma at the Cotton Bowl. The biggest positive involves running back Hollywood Smothers, who missed the Tennessee game despite dressing in an emergency role. MORE: Ex Texas Star Wins NFL Rookie Honor Steve Sarkisian indicated after the 20-17 win that Smothers was close enough to play if absolutely necessary. The following bye week gave Texas additional time to get its leading rusher healthy. That could matter considerably against Oklahoma. Smothers leads Texas with 198 rushing yards on 41 carries and gives the Longhorns another physical option alongside Raleek Brown and Derrek Cooper. Texas managed without him at Tennessee, but getting Smothers back would make life considerably easier for quarterback Arch Manning. Wide receiver Cam Coleman also appears to be trending toward full availability after suffering a bruised tailbone against Tennessee. Coleman returned to that game, and Sarkisian described the injury as nothing serious. His presence opposite Ryan Wingo is important because Texas needs its vertical passing game intact against an Oklahoma defense likely to challenge Manning with pressure and disguised coverages. The bigger uncertainty may be on defense. Terry’s status could be particularly important. Oklahoma’s offense will test Texas between the tackles, and having another disruptive interior lineman would allow the Longhorns to keep their defensive front fresh while freeing star edge rusher Colin Simmons to attack the quarterback. Simmons dealt with wrist and elbow discomfort against Tennessee but returned to the game and is not currently expected to miss Oklahoma. MORE: Texas Longhorns Visit 5-Star WR Commit Amid Bye Week, Flip Buzz Texas is 4-0 and ranked No. 1 entering Saturday’s 2:30 p.m. CT matchup in Dallas. The Longhorns have won the past two Red River meetings by a combined 57-9, including a 23-6 victory last season. Still, rivalry games rarely follow the script.
