picks.headline: Early preview of No. 23 UCLA Bruins ahead of Oregon Ducks showdown
picks.blurb: Early preview of No. 23 UCLA Bruins ahead of Oregon Ducks showdown - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Week 5 Waiver Wire NFL Power Rankings Gauff decries racist posts Messi's Argentina finale Falcons run over Saints Early preview of No. 23 UCLA Bruins ahead of Oregon Ducks showdown Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Oregon Ducks are in the midst of a much-needed bye week, enjoying some time off after a strenuous and pressure-filled first month of the 2026 season. Through four games, we've seen the Ducks start at No. 2 in the AP poll, drop to No. 6 after an underwhelming win over Boise State before losing to Oklahoma State, dropping them all the way down to No. 21. They then took care of Portland State, 84-0, moving them up a spot before a pivotal road matchup in Los Angeles with USC . The Ducks never blinked, even when quarterback Dante Moore had to leave the game via ambulance with a head injury, as backup Dylan Raiola and some timely defensive plays powered Oregon over USC, 41-27. It was as impressive of a win as we've seen from the Ducks over the past two seasons, and one that they badly needed in order to keep their goals of winning a national championship alive. Now, Oregon gets to take a breath and relax with a Week 5 bye. But that's not all that the players and staff are doing, as they'll be getting a jumpstart on preparing for the upstart UCLA Bruins , who will come to town in Week 6. We'll follow suit, providing an early deep-dive preview of how the Bruins ' season has gone so far, a breakdown of the offense, defense, special teams and players to watch with game and betting details to boot. Let's start with UCLA's resume, as they head into the matchup with Oregon looking to continue their undefeated season. UCLA's Resume Through Five Weeks Sep 26, 2026; College Park, Maryland, USA; UCLA Bruins wide receiver Aidan Mizell (1) dances in the end zone with wide receiver Landon Ellis (11) and wide receiver Semaj Morgan (4) after catching an 83-yard touchdown reception in the second half against the Maryland Terrapins at SECU Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Jamie Sabau-Imagn Images Week 1: W 45-24 @ Cal Week 2: W 28-10 vs. San Diego State Week 3: W 52-38 vs. Purdue Week 4: W 52-3 @ Maryland The Bruins got off to an impressive start in the newly-hired Bob Chesney era, taking down the Tosh Lupoi-led Golden Bears on the road after a dominant second half. Chesney, who commanded James Madison to the College Football Playoff a year ago, relied upon several of his former Dukes that followed him to Westwood in the season-opener. The start of the season was strong, and so was last game for UCLA. The Bruins went into Maryland and stomped all over the Terrapins, picking off four passes and racking up 475 total yards. The early, 10:30 PT start didn't hold them back, as they jumped out to a 20-3 lead at halftime and only added to the lead after the break. Sandwiched between those two spectacular outings were victories over San Diego State and Purdue, with the offense carrying them in the former and offense in the latter, showing how well-rounded the Bruins are in 2026. Offensive Breakdown Sep 26, 2026; College Park, Maryland, USA; UCLA Bruins running back Jaivian Thomas (21) celebrates with offensive line Hall Schmidt (65) after scoring a touchdown in the first half against the Maryland Terrapins at SECU Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Jamie Sabau-Imagn Images While last season was discombobulated at times for the Bruins offensively, new coordinator Dean Kennedy — coming over with Chesney from James Madison — has brought a revitalized, intelligent and, thus far, highly-successful offense to UCLA. Kennedy has a history of elevating previously subpar offensive units, as he developed quarterback Kyle Trask at Florida, turned Holy Cross into the Patriot League scoring leader and orchestrated the ninth-ranked scoring offense at James Madison in 2025. Now, he's doing the same thing at UCLA with a spread-based system that emphasizes physicality and explosiveness at the point of attack. Kennedy's units have consistently been among the best at creating explosive plays, both on the ground and through the air. While the Bruins won't go under center much at all, instead standing in the shotgun or pistol, they aren't afraid to run it right down the defense's throat. Through the air, the route combinations aren't necessarily complex, but they make it easy on the quarterback to read with a progression-based system. Defensive Breakdown Sep 26, 2026; College Park, Maryland, USA; UCLA Bruins linebacker Trent Hendrick (25) celebrates after intercepting a pass in the second half against the Maryland Terrapins at SECU Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Jamie Sabau-Imagn Images Also brought over from James Madison, Colin Hitschler is the defensive coordinator for the Bruins with a goal of instilling an uncommon physicality that hasn't been seen in Westwood for some time. And thus far this fall, UCLA has, for the most part, lived up those goals. The Bruins mostly operate out of a 4-2-5 defensive alignment, following the trend of opting to put an extra defensive back on the field over a lumbering linebacker. But make no mistake, the linebackers have plenty of talent to handle the middle of the field themselves, with a pair of seniors coming in at first and second on the team in tackles through four games. Hitschler isn't afraid to send pressure, having loads of success against Maryland in forcing the quarterback to make decisions under duress that turned into four interceptions. Expect more of the same come Week 6, with Hitschler putting the onus on the offensive line to protect whoever trots out at quarterback for the Ducks. Special Teams Breakdown Sep 12, 2026; Pasadena, California, USA; UCLA kicker Mateen Bhaghani (15) kicks a field-goal during the second half against San Diego State at the Rose Bowl. Mandatory Credit: William Liang-Imagn Images The Bruins have modest special teams units, with average kickoff and punt return marks with the same for the coverage units — though the return aspect could change in a blink with a pair of return men with elite speed waiting back there. In the kicking game, kicker Mateen Bhaghani has been solid in converting 4-of-5 field goals and all 23 extra points. It's his third season as the starter at UCLA, and he's made 82.8% of his field goals with a long of 57 yards — a massive advantage at the college level. Punter Curtis Gerrand also has a big leg, averaging 45.7 yards per punt on 15 boots thus far. Players to Watch Sep 26, 2026; College Park, Maryland, USA; UCLA Bruins quarterback Nico Iamaleava (9) passes in the first half against the Maryland Terrapins at SECU Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Jamie Sabau-Imagn Images There's an abundance of talent across the roster, yet these three players will have to be accounted for by the Ducks if they're to get their fourth win. QB Nico Iamaleava 2026 Season Stats: 62-for-99, 820 yards, 4 TDs, 2 INTs / / 35 rushes, 143 yards, 1 TD Analysis: Iamaleava hasn't quite needed to show off his world-class athleticism this year, with his backfield mate stealing much of the thunder in the first month of the season. That's not to say the former Tennessee starter can't scoot, as he's run for 1,077 yards and 11 touchdowns in four seasons while tossing 38 touchdowns and 14 interceptions. Not the most refined passer, Iamaleava — like many college quarterbacks — feasts on short and long throws, but hasn't quite developed the intermediate aspect of his game. Still very talented, Iamaleava is commanding mid-to-late round draft buzz, though he does have one more season of eligibility remaining. RB Wayne Knight 2026 Season Stats: 49 rushes, 445 yards, 9 TDs / / 8 catches, 88 yards Analysis: Yes, you read that right. Wayne has nine touchdowns four games into the year, with six coming in the first two games. Standing just 5-foot-7 and 193 pounds, Knight makes up for his lack of size with elite speed, vision and playmaking ability. At James Madison in 2025, Knight broke off runs of 73, 59, 58 and 49 yards with 57 and 49-yard gains on receptions. Always an ability to hit a home-run, the Ducks will have to be cognizant not to lose Knight behind the Bruins' offensive line. LB Sammy Omosigho 2026 Season Stats: 37 tackles, 3 sacks, 4 forced fumbles Analysis: Though the Bruins added 2025 Sun Belt Defensive Player of the Year Trent Hendricks to the roster recently, he's still getting acclimated so we'll spotlight Sammy Omosigho here. The 6-foot-2, 239-pound four-year Oklahoma transfer has gotten off to a fast start at UCLA, leading the team in tackles and recording three sacks from his linebacker spot. Hitschler sends the former Sooner quite often on pressures and he makes plays as evidenced by his four forced fumbles in four games. When former Dukes coach Bob Chesney made the move to Los Angeles in December, he brought 11 players and almost his entire coaching staff with him. Several of those players are now starting for the No. 22 Bruins (4-0, 2-0 Big Ten), who will be at Autzen Stadium Oct. 10 for a 12:30 p.m. conference game against No. 13 Oregon (3-1, 1-0). (Ben Lonergan/The Register-Guard) 1 / 12 See photos as Oregon Ducks football opens Big Ten play at USC Trojans See photos as Oregon Ducks football opens Big Ten play at USC Trojans Grading every Oregon Ducks football unit during 2026 bye week Dante Moore shares heartfelt social media message following head injury What Oregon football's 41-27 win over USC means heading into bye week "JMUCLA," is how UCLA tight end and James Madison transfer Josh Phifer described his new team earlier this season. Chesney has his new team rolling. Like the Ducks , the Bruins are coming off a bye week . In their last game, they defeated Maryland 54-3 on Sept. 26 and held the Terrapins to 181 yards and one first-half field goal. Chesney's last game at James Madison came at Autzen Stadium on Dec. 20 when Oregon won 51-34 in a College Football Playoff first-round game. Eight starters for JMU in that game are now at UCLA. Here's an early look at the Bruins. Who is UCLA's QB? Nico Iamaleava is thriving in his second season as the Bruins' starter. The 6-5, 215-pound senior, who was the nation's No. 1 overall recruit in 2023, has thrown for 820 yards and four touchdowns, and has rushed for 143 and one TD. Last year he was one-man show at UCLA when he threw for 1,928 yards and 13 touchdowns with seven interceptions while also leading the Bruins in rushing yards (505), carries (112) and rushing touchdowns (4). Other UCLA offensive standouts Running back Wayne Knight is second in the Big Ten with 445 rushing yards and leads the conference with nine rushing touchdowns. The former James Madison star is averaging 9.1 yards per carry and 111.3 per game. The 5-7, 193-pound fifth year was a second-team All-American in 2025 after totaling 2,039 all-purpose yards. Michigan transfer Semaj Morgan is the Bruins' top receiver with 14 receptions for 174 yards and two touchdowns – all team highs. Defensive standouts for UCLA Senior linebacker Sammy Omosigho has been terrorizing opposing offenses this season. The transfer from Oklahoma leads the Bruins with 40 tackles (27 solo), 7.5 tackles for loss, three sacks and four forced fumbles. Safety Ta'Shawn James, a transfer from Iowa State, has 24 tackles and a conference-leading three interceptions, including a pick-six against Maryland. Former Oregon reserve Rodrick Pleasant is in his second season starting at cornerback for UCLA. He was all-Big Ten honorable mention in 2025. The last time the Ducks and Bruins met Oregon defeated UCLA 34-13 at the Rose Bowl on Sept. 28, 2024, in what was the Ducks' first conference game as a member of the Big Ten. They led 28-10 at halftime and the only touchdown of the game for the Bruins came on an interception return in the second quarter. Notes: Oregon has won five straight against UCLA dating back to the 2018 season. ... The Ducks are 16-3 against the Bruins since 2000 and have won 11 of the last 12 matchups. ... UCLA has only one win at Autzen Stadium since 1998. That came in the 2004 season. ... UCLA has opened the season with a 4-0 record for the first time since 2022 when it won its first five games. That was also the last time the Bruins had a five-game winning streak. It’s the first ranked Big Ten opponent to visit Eugene this season. The Ducks’ biggest question is at quarterback. Dante Moore (926 yards, nine touchdowns, 69.7% completions) suffered a concussion on a targeting hit in the 41-27 win at USC and remains in concussion protocol with no set return date. If Moore can’t go, former Nebraska starter Dylan Raiola gets the start. Raiola took over at USC and led Oregon to points on six of seven drives. Dan Lanning has said the team is taking “an abundance of caution” with Moore. Whoever starts will face one of the most opportunistic defenses in the country. Defensive coordinator Colin Hitschler’s 3-3-5 stack moves after the snap, and UCLA leads the Big Ten with eight interceptions. Six different Bruins have an interception, led by Ta’Shawn James with three, and UCLA is tied for the conference lead with five forced fumbles. The Bruins also have plenty of motivation. First-year coach Bob Chesney brought his James Madison team to Autzen last season and lost 51-34 after falling behind 34-6 at halftime. Ten former Dukes are on his first UCLA roster. Quarterback Nico Iamaleava is averaging a career-high 8.3 yards per play, and the Bruins scored 52 points against Purdue and 54 at Maryland in back-to-back weeks. away.headline: Oregon Gets Encouraging Dante Moore Injury Update Ahead of UCLA
away.blurb: USA TODAY's Jordan Mendoza reported that Oregon coach Dan Lanning said Moore was "wearing a helmet and shoulder pads today and was out there throwing the football." Lanning wasn't ready to reveal where Moore stands in the concussion protocol or whether he will be available against the Bruins. "Dante was out there at practice for us today," Lanning said, via CBS Sports' Austin Nivison . "Similar to what we said before, we're gonna do what's best for Dante moving forward. … It was great to see him back out there with his teammates getting to work today." Dante Moore Could Return Against Former Team UCLA The timing makes Moore's potential return even more interesting. "Dylan's got to keep doing what he's been doing," Lanning said. Stephens was ejected for targeting, while Moore was taken off the field on a stretcher and transported to a Los Angeles hospital. Oregon later confirmed that Moore had movement in all of his extremities and had suffered a concussion. Oregon heads into the second half of the season at 3-1 overall and 1-0 in Big Ten play, with its only loss coming on the road at Oklahoma State. The Ducks followed that up by crushing Portland State 84-0 before rallying behind Raiola to beat USC in LA. home.headline: Cal-UNLV Thread: New-Look Bears Lose JKS to Injury, Trail 24-7 at Halftime
home.blurb: Cal quarterback Jaron-Keawe Sagapolutele hands off to running back Adam Mohammed, whose status is questionable for UNLV | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Jeff Faraudo Sat, October 3, 2026 at 6:42 PM UTC · 8 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads Cal closes out its non-conference schedule this afternoon at UNLV in its first road meeting vs. the Rebels. Kickoff is 12:30 p.m. The forecast calls for 92 degrees at kickoff with the temperature climbing to about 96 by mid-afternoon, so Bears will be relieved the game is played indoors. Injury update: Cal announces Ashten Emory as starting running back, meaning Adam Mohammed will not be available after sustaining a knee injury vs. Clemson last Friday night. 12:10 1st Q: Cal safety Kingston Lopa, who leads the nation with five interceptions, goes down with an apparent injury and is helped off the field. Would be a big loss to the Bears' defense if he cannot return. Cal 0, UNLV 0 11:30 1st Q: Cal forces a 3-and-out and takes over at the 9-yard line after a UNLV punt. Jaron-Keawe Sagapolutele completes a pass to freshman TE Taimane Purcell -- a fellow native of Hawaii -- and Purcell spins away from a would-be tackler and races 91 yards to the end zone. A one-play, 91-yard scooring drive and Cal's first offensive touchdown since two weeks ago vs. Wagner. Just Purcell's fourth catch of the season and his first collegiate touchdown. Cal 7, UNLV 0 11:25 1st Q: Cal kicks off and Cal's Cam Sidney, the Bears' starting nickel, is flagged for targeting for a helmet-to-helmet on return man Peyton Zachary. Sidney is ejected and will miss the first half of next week's game vs. Virginia Tech. Bears now without two starting DBs, with Lopa will on the sideline. Cal 7, UNLV 0 0:34 1st: On second-and-10 from the UNLV 28 after Aidan Manutai partially blocked a UNLV punt, JKS is pressured and forced to the right. Makes ill-advised throw that is picked off by Quandarius Keyes and return 44 yards to the Bears' 28-yard line. Cal 7, UNLV 0 3:36 3rd Q: Niles Davis recovers a fumble by Peyton Zachary on the kickoff return, giving Cal possession at the 16-yard line. The Bears cannot cash it in for a TD but Chase Meyer converts a 38-yard field goal. Cal is coming off a 24-10 home defeat to Clemson, which held the Bears without an offensive touchdown at Memorial Stadium for the first time since 2018. Finding an offensive rhythm may be complicated by player availability. Running backs Adam Mohammed and Carter Vargas are question to play due to injuries. Kalshi has it as close to a coin flip, but my Georgia vs. Alabama prediction and college football picks lean toward the Bulldogs in a rock fight on Saturday, Oct. 10 at 7:30 p.m. ET on ABC. Georgia vs Alabama predictions For help understanding Kalshi probabilities, see our odds calculator . Percentages courtesy of Kalshi , one of the best prediction market apps . Early Georgia vs Alabama spread pick: Georgia +1.5 Kalshi probability: 49% This is the best defense Keelon Russell has faced. Alabama's first-year starter has been excellent lately, with 13 touchdowns and no turnovers in his last three games. However, those games came against Florida State, South Carolina, and Mississippi State. Georgia allows just 57.4 rushing yards per game, third-best in the country. If that holds, Alabama's offense will rest almost entirely on Russell's arm. On the other side, Gunner Stockton is a fifth-year senior. He's 17-3 as a starter, 6-2 against ranked teams, and third nationally in passing efficiency at 202.0. He gets an Alabama pass defense that allows 234 yards per game , ranking 14th in the SEC. Stockton also protects the ball: he has just eight interceptions in 571 career attempts . That matters against a Tide defense that leads the SEC with 13 takeaways. Georgia usually starts fast, outscoring opponents 70-7 in the first quarter. That's a problem for Alabama, because Kalen DeBoer is 1-7 at Alabama when trailing at halftime. Yes, Kirby Smart is 0-7 against Alabama in the regular season, and DeBoer is 16-1 at Bryant-Denny. But the last time these teams met, Georgia won the SEC title game 28-7. I'll take the points with the more experienced quarterback. Start trading with Kalshi today! Georgia's 51.4 points per game includes Tennessee State and Western Kentucky. Alabama's 49.6 points per game came against East Carolina, Kentucky, Florida State, South Carolina, and Mississippi State. Both defenses stop the run. Georgia allows 57.4 rushing yards per game and Alabama 78.6 (10th nationally), so long drives will be hard to sustain. Alabama is also allowing just 6.4 points per game after halftime, and opponents convert only 27.5% of their third downs against the Tide (15th nationally). The last two meetings totaled 45 and 35 points. The biggest risk to the Under is a defensive score, since Alabama has already returned four interceptions for touchdowns. Still, I expect a tighter, field-position game than the season averages suggest. picks.headline: Georgia @ Alabama Preview And Prediction
picks.blurb: Georgia @ Alabama Preview And Prediction - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Week 5 Waiver Wire NFL Power Rankings Gauff decries racist posts Messi's Argentina finale Falcons run over Saints Georgia @ Alabama Preview And Prediction Photo Credit: David Leong Landon Kardian Tue, October 6, 2026 at 3:25 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads It does not get much bigger than this. No. 2 Georgia travels to Tuscaloosa Saturday night to face No. 6 Alabama in a 7:30 p.m. kickoff at Bryant-Denny Stadium. Both teams enter 5-0 and 3-0 in SEC play, making this one of the biggest games of the college football season. Georgia absolutely has a path to winning this game. The Bulldogs have the more experienced quarterback in Gunner Stockton, an elite rushing attack and a defense allowing just 13.4 points per game. Stockton has completed 75.5% of his passes with 13 touchdowns and only one interception. But there is one major concern: Can Georgia's defense get enough stops? Keelon Russell has been on fire. He has thrown for 1,414 yards with 11 touchdowns and just two interceptions while adding another four touchdowns on the ground. Alabama just went into Starkville and dropped 56 points on Mississippi State, with Russell throwing for 285 yards and three touchdowns. Georgia's defense has been good statistically, but it hasn't faced anything quite like this Alabama offense. The Bulldogs showed some cracks against Vanderbilt, allowing 293 yards and struggling to consistently get off the field on third down before tightening things up in the second half. Against Russell, those mistakes could become touchdowns. Georgia's best chance is to run the football, control possession and keep Russell standing on the Alabama sideline. Nate Frazier and the Bulldogs' offensive line can absolutely have success, and Stockton's efficiency gives Georgia another way to move the football if Alabama loads the box. The problem is that Alabama can counter by bringing pressure and trusting its secondary. Kirby Smart called Alabama's defensive backs talented, physical "ball hawks" and specifically pointed to the pressure created by the Crimson Tide's front. And then there is Bryant-Denny Stadium . This game being in Tuscaloosa matters. Georgia will be dealing with one of the loudest environments in college football against an Alabama team playing with a ton of confidence. Even the betting market has shifted toward the Crimson Tide, with Alabama currently sitting around a 1.5-point favorite after Georgia initially opened as the favorite. Prediction: Alabama 38, Georgia 27 I trust Georgia to move the football. I trust Stockton's experience, and I think the Bulldogs can establish the run. I just don't trust Georgia to get enough stops. Russell's ability to create outside structure is the difference. Georgia can defend the play perfectly and still watch Russell escape the pocket and turn it into an explosive gain. Add the home-field advantage, Alabama's veteran secondary and the Tide's ability to pressure Stockton, and the matchup starts leaning toward Bama. Georgia hangs around, but eventually Russell makes too many plays. Alabama 38, Georgia 27. Check Out All EasySportz College Football Content Here! College Football Viewing Guide
